title: bug: daemon/proxy path comparison folds POSIX case on Windows and disagrees with UNC identity rules
description:
Adversarial review of task-e7f4026a found pre-existing comparableProjectPath drift in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts and the daemon twin: Windows node maps /home/qa/OtherProject and /home/qa/otherproject to the same c:/home/qa/otherproject, while launcher/JetBrains preserve POSIX case.
Linux proxy also gives different keys for \\srv\share\proj vs //SRV/SHARE/PROJ/; WSL UNC \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\u\proj vs /home/u/proj differs on both OSes although Kotlin maps it. Pure helper repro against b2138fba built bytes: /tmp/e7f4-resume.mvnO0m/{path-parity.mjs,linux-path-parity.log,windows-path-parity.log}; Windows harness C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/e7f4-resume.IXcXBP/path-parity.mjs.
Keep this outside the current launcher QA fix; define one cross-platform comparison contract and add Linux/native-Windows regressions before changing shared utilities.
definitionOfDone: Case-distinct absolute POSIX served paths do not compare equal solely because the client runs on Windows.
UNC and WSL-share equivalence rules are explicit and tested against the launcher and JetBrains rules.
Proxy/daemon identity and discovery suites cover the corrected comparison on Linux and native Windows without regressing drive-/mnt spellings.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST, then the rule (load test-driven-development). Never run npm test, npm run build or vitest in the shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy: live WSL seats run its dist/ through the global npm link, and its node_modules are Windows builds (mem:gotcha-proxy-npm-test-shared-checkout-deletes-dist). Edit the worktree, and iterate in a /tmp snapshot (recipe in step 5).

Contested path: task-724e31fa's plan also names utils.ts, for its getDaemonHost JSDoc only; leave that JSDoc alone.
- Run moe.get_commit_scope {taskId, phase:'postflight'} and read peerDeclared.
- A contested path lands only when a wrapper-witnessed editor wrote it (Claude Edit/Write, or Serena's editors), or when it was clean at this session's pre-flight and every contesting task is idle.
- A seat with no witnessed editor finishes all its edits to such a path in one session.
- If the session-ended line names held=<path>, follow its MOE_CONTESTED_HELD remedy. Never hand-land the path or weaken the policy.

A. packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts, in describe('comparableProjectPath'). Reuse onWin32, hoisting it to file scope if the readDaemonInfo row needs it. Keep every existing test unchanged: they are the drive, /mnt and relative-path regressions.
1. A contract table of [input, key] rows. Assert it with one toEqual natively and once more under onWin32; identical keys on both prove the rule is OS-independent.
- D:\proj → d:/proj; d:/Proj/ → d:/proj; D:\ → d:; D:/../proj → d:/proj
- /mnt/d/proj → d:/proj; /mnt/D/Proj/ → d:/proj; /mnt/d → d:; /mnt/dd/x → /mnt/dd/x; /MNT/d/x → /MNT/d/x
- /home/qa/OtherProject → /home/qa/OtherProject; /home/qa/otherproject → /home/qa/otherproject; /home//u/./x/../p/ → /home/u/p; ///x → /x
- \\srv\share\proj → //srv/share/proj; //SRV/SHARE/PROJ/ → //srv/share/proj; //srv/share/../../b → //srv/share/b
- \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\u\proj → /home/u/proj; //wsl$/Ubuntu/home/u/proj → /home/u/proj; //WSL$/Ubuntu/mnt/d/proj → d:/proj; //wsl$/Ubuntu → /
- 'D:/qa/\u212a' → d:/qa/k. This is the documented toLowerCase fold, the same as Kotlin lowercase() and python lower().
2. DoD 1, under onWin32: /home/u/p and C:\home\u\p get different keys. No cwd drive is added to a POSIX path.
3. Drive letter and mount are ASCII-only. '\u212a:/x' is not a drive: its key differs from k:/x. '/mnt/\u212a/x' keeps the key /mnt/\u212a/x.
4. Discovery: write a .moe/daemon.json whose projectPath is testDir.toUpperCase().
- POSIX testDir: readDaemonInfoResult(testDir) returns the error 'daemon.json belongs to a different project', natively and under onWin32.
- Drive testDir (native Windows): it returns the info, because drive paths stay case-insensitive.
- Branch on testDir's form, not on process.platform.
Run A against HEAD's utils.ts first. Expect assertion failures from the UNC and WSL rows natively on Linux, and from the POSIX-case rows under onWin32.

B. packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts: replace comparableProjectPath and normalizeWindowsDrivePath. Port Kotlin DaemonIdentityProbe.comparableProjectPath, classified by the launchers' regex:
- WINDOWS_FORM = /^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|[\\/]{2}[^\\/])/: drive or UNC, as in moe-agent.{sh,ps1} and the daemon's isForeignDaemonInfo.
- WSL_SHARE = /^\/\/(?:wsl\$|wsl\.localhost)\/[^/]+(\/.*)?$/i: no u flag, so ASCII-only.
- MNT_DRIVE = /^\/mnt\/([A-Za-z])(?:\/(.*))?$/
comparableProjectPath(p):
- raw = p.trim().
- abs = raw when WINDOWS_FORM matches it or it starts with '/'; otherwise path.resolve(raw).
- If WINDOWS_FORM does not match abs, return posixKey(abs).
- Otherwise let s be abs with every \ turned into /. On a WSL_SHARE match, return posixKey(group 1 ?? '/').
- Otherwise unc = s.startsWith('//'). Return (unc ? '//' : '') + collapse(s, unc ? 2 : 1), lowercased.
posixKey(p): key = '/' + collapse(p, 0). On a MNT_DRIVE match, return `${letter}:${rest ? '/' + rest : ''}` lowercased; otherwise return the key with its case kept.
collapse(p, keep): split on '/' and drop '' and '.' segments. '..' pops only while more than keep segments remain (the drive, or the UNC server and share). Join with '/'.
The absolute route has no process.platform branch and no path.win32 or path.posix normalize. Only a relative input reaches path.resolve, which keeps native cwd semantics and the X9 and cwd-spy rows.
Error handling: the rule stays a total, pure string function. It does no IO and never throws for any string input; path.resolve sees only relative input. readDaemonInfoResult keeps its existing error results and messages unchanged.
The doc comment IS the contract, at most about 22 lines. It must state:
- who follows it: the daemon twin, JetBrains DaemonIdentityProbe and the launchers;
- the three forms and their separators;
- the '..' floor;
- case: drive and UNC fold with toLowerCase (locale-independent, full Unicode; it over-folds U+212A and U+212B, which NTFS keeps apart, a fail-open 'same'), and POSIX keeps case;
- the drive letter and mount are ASCII-only, and the distro is not compared;
- a relative input is resolved first;
- the launchers still read a WSL share as plain UNC until task-3def0804.
Run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in the snapshot, because tsc compiles the tests too.

comments.content:
QA input from the task-e7f4026a reopen-1 review (qa-952969be, 2026-10-30), for the shared path rule. This is non-blocking. I ran a 46-row table through the REAL ps1 Get-MoeDaemonIdentity on PS5.1 and PS7 against a fake /health, and through the sh probe's python comparable() on Linux and Windows python. Every realistic same-project spelling and every distinct-project row agrees across engines. The exotic divergences all come from Unicode case-folding:
(1) 'D:/qa/\u00c5' vs 'D:/qa/\u212b' (Angstrom sign), and 'D:/qa/K' vs 'D:/qa/\u212a' (Kelvin sign): python and PS7 say same; PS5.1 says foreign. NTFS's upcase table treats these as distinct names, so lowercasing over-folds.
(2) ps1's case-insensitive -match/-notmatch on [A-Za-z] accepts a Kelvin-sign 'drive' ('\u212a:/x'): PS says foreign or same where sh/proxy say unknown.
Neither yields a realistic wrong adoption, but a defined shared rule (upcase vs lowercase, ASCII-only drive class) would settle both. Table and runner: /tmp/qa952-e7f4.xiPE0L/probe/{windows-table.txt,linux-table.txt,runner.mjs,rows.mjs}.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
moe-proxy comparableProjectPath (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts) and its daemon twin (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts) give every absolute project path a key that does not depend on the OS computing it.
- Drive and UNC forms: \ and / both separate, '..' never climbs past the drive or the UNC server and share, and case folds with toLowerCase.
- \\wsl$\<distro>\x and \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\x name that distro's POSIX /x.
- Any other path starting with / is POSIX: it keeps its case and maps /mnt/<d>[/x] to <d>:[/x].
- Only a relative path is first resolved natively against cwd.
Tests prove this natively, under win32 emulation and on native Windows. They also check the proxy, daemon, sh and ps1 launcher, and JetBrains rules against one table.
acceptanceCriteria: On Linux, under onWin32 emulation and on native Windows, /home/qa/OtherProject and /home/qa/otherproject get distinct keys, and /home/u/p differs from C:\home\u\p.

On every OS, \\srv\share\proj and //SRV/SHARE/PROJ/ share the key //srv/share/proj. \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\u\proj, //wsl$/Ubuntu/home/u/proj and /home/u/proj share /home/u/proj. //WSL$/Ubuntu/mnt/d/proj equals D:\proj.

Drive and /mnt spellings keep their HEAD keys: D:\x, d:/x/ and /mnt/d/x all give d:/x. Relative and non-normalized inputs keep their HEAD verdicts: X9, X11 and the proxy cwd-spy rows are unchanged and pass.
probeDaemonIdentity classifies served /home/qa/OtherProject against own /home/qa/otherproject as foreign, and the UNC and WSL-share spellings as same, natively on Linux and on Windows.

Both dists give every path-contract row its key and match every absolute row of the JetBrains comparableProjectPath table. The sh and ps1 launcher rules match every non-WSL-share row. The launchers' WSL-share rows are todo, naming task-3def0804.
invariants: comparableProjectPath output is comparison-only and is never written to disk.
comparableProjectPath never throws for any string input.
isForeignDaemonInfo and every daemon.json and daemon.lock deleter are unchanged.
The absolute-path route has no process.platform branch; path.resolve runs only for a relative input.
Existing tests stay byte-identical, except that the X1 win32 guard is removed and rows are added.
compatibility: The signatures of comparableProjectPath(projectPath: string): string and isSameProjectPath are unchanged. The daemon adds comparableProjectPath to its named exports.
The daemon.json, daemon.lock and /health shapes, and every MCP tool contract, are unchanged.
The launchers, JetBrains, VS Code (task-80ed1fe8, now dependsOn this task) and scripts/local-runner are not edited.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Keep path.resolve for POSIX input on win32 and only skip the lowercase: rejected. It still prefixes the cwd drive, so /home/u/p would equal C:\home\u\p on Windows.
- Port Kotlin byte for byte: rejected for classification. Kotlin reads ///x as UNC, lowercasing a POSIX path (a false foreign, the destructive direction), and treats \ as a separator inside POSIX paths. The launchers' regex, which QA's 46-row table validated on PS5.1, PS7 and python, is used instead. Kotlin's WSL-share mapping is kept.
- Read a WSL share as plain UNC (the launcher rule): rejected. It breaks the \\wsl$ IDE workflow in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and makes the \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost aliases of one share compare foreign. The launchers follow in task-3def0804.
- ASCII-only case folding: rejected. It would make D:/É vs D:/é a false foreign. toLowerCase agrees with Kotlin lowercase(), python lower() and PS7.
- A shared JSON fixture read by Kotlin, TS and the launchers: rejected, because it means Kotlin edits plus a gradle run. Parsing the Kotlin test table from the scripts test gives the same drift guard without touching Kotlin.
- Adding the vitest suites to Windows CI: rejected, because index.test.ts's Windows status is unknown. The scripts contract test already runs in Linux and Windows CI and imports both dists. The worker runs the vitest suites natively on Windows once.

- The 400-net-LOC QA cap counts tests; the planned budget is about 240.
- Contested paths: task-724e31fa names utils.ts (its getDaemonHost JSDoc), and task-3def0804 will name daemon-json-cap.test.mjs.
- Child-process imports of the dists must exit explicitly.
- PS5.1 needs a BOM'd script.

Preserve live-lock exclusion for native aliases without weakening cross-OS foreign-daemon protections.
